key_insight: GraphVid introduces a graph-based way to control video generation, making it easier to specify precise interactions among multiple objects than text prompts or simple motion trajectories. This enables more flexible and less ambiguous multi-subject control, especially in complex scenes with overlap or occlusion.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of controlling video generation for multiple interacting objects using text or trajectory-based inputs, which are often too vague, hard to scale, and ambiguous when objects overlap or are occluded.
method: Represents scene control as a graph, allowing users to define object relationships and interactions more precisely than with free-form text.
Uses graph-conditioned video generation to translate structured control signals into coherent video outputs.
Supports multi-object scenarios where trajectory drawing alone becomes impractical or ambiguous.
impact: GraphVid could make controllable video generation more practical for researchers and practitioners who need fine-grained scene editing, animation, or simulation. It improves usability in complex scenes by giving users a clearer and more scalable control interface.
visual_elements: A side-by-side comparison of text prompt control vs trajectory control vs graph control
A node-and-edge scene graph showing multiple objects and their interactions
A before/after video frame sequence demonstrating controllable motion and object relationships
An icon set for objects, connections, and occlusion to illustrate ambiguity reduction
paper_authors: Vedant Shah, Onkar Susladkar, Tushar Prakash, Kiet Nguyen, Tianjio Yu
